Params: Before the Sefirah Engine, Rusalka crashes to her knees on the ground ravaged by cannon fire and lightning whips.
Piece by piece, her helmet splinters apart with a fine crackling sound.
Adelyde is pulled down with Rusalka before she can react. The red-clad Construct's vision swims in and out, and she forces her exhausted frame back to consciousness.
Her eyes dart frantically across those green irises.
Rusalka, is that you? Don't let Arius control you!
What is your head made of... That really hurt...
Her right hand shifts, slipping free from the shocked Adelyde's loosened grip. Raising it toward Adelyde, Rusalka hesitates halfway.
She seems to have rehearsed this a thousand times in her mind, but never once did she dare to do it.
Those sharp claws, for the very first time, cradle the side of Adelyde's face.
That was never what I was fighting for!
Does having different beliefs and being on opposite sides mean you have to throw the other person away and make it all about winning?
Her voice breaks as she forces the words out between her gritted teeth.
I gave it all I had... just for a few more chances to see you...
I'm afraid I can't even give you that.
Rusalka looks down at her left arm, the one that bore the brunt of their clash. Adelyde follows her gaze, and the Construct's expression instantly goes blank.
At the ragged edges of her damaged limb, luminous blue and blood-red fluid weave together, repairing her frame at an alarming speed.
The strange red light that once spread around her eyes has reappeared on her arm.
I've locked down my arm, but it's spreading.
When it takes my mind again, you won't be able to pull the same trick twice.
Besides, I'm rather fond of this body. I'm not quite ready to give it up just yet.
The Ascendant's voice comes from one of the mechanical giant phantom jelly's tentacles. He perches there, sounding irritated for some reason.
I couldn't even if I wanted to.
The moment I withdraw my power, her mind will collapse. You should be asking her what she did to her own mind.
A single word is all it takes to calm Adelyde. Rusalka looks up at Arius.
You've been living rent-free in my head long enough. The least you can do is stay quiet for once here at the end.
I'd still prefer you change your mind, my "half-creation."
She turns to the frowning Adelyde, drawing her student's attention back to her.
Arius did rebuild this frame, that much is true. But he honored the original design in the one place he shouldn't have... he kept the self-destruct mechanism I built for myself.
At first, it was to prevent me from failing a mission. Later, it was to keep the old wolves in the family from getting inside my head after the cybernetic modifications.
My loyalty belongs to me alone. My free will is the one thing I cannot afford to lose, and I intend to keep it that way until my last breath.
You woke me, and in doing so, you gave me that. I'm grateful.
Adelyde cannot say a single word. Gripping Rusalka's shoulders, she just keeps shaking her head.
Don't let your memory paint me in a kinder light than I deserve. And don't regret your choices.
You'll always carry the best of me within you. You'll always carry the lost belief and glory of the TEC.
Let them echo through you, unto the ages of ages.
She looks past Adelyde and gives you a single, quiet nod.
Adelyde, will you come with me?
(Steady Adelyde by the shoulders and gently guide her back)
Adelyde pries her fingers from Rusalka's shoulders, as though it costs her every last ounce of will she has.
She stands shakily, steadying herself one step at a time before turning around. Chin raised and unflinching, she makes her declaration to Rusalka.
You and everyone will witness my voyage on the other side... Until we meet again.
A white energy pulse as gentle as seafoam blooms from Rusalka's chest, spreading across her entire body.
The fluid and red light that once wreathed her dissolve into the seafoam along with her frame. She becomes a tangible breath of wind, drifting toward Ananke's light.
Like a river finding the sea, she returns to the flow of time.
Like a river finding the sea, she returns to the flow of time.
The Ascendant's sigh drifts through the chamber like a ghost.
Of all the things beyond my understanding, humanity's obsession with self-destruction is the one that eludes me most.
Years of careful cultivation, thrown away in an instant. And rather than reflecting on it, you dress up this reckless impulse as conviction...
Expecting you people to listen to reason is like scrubbing rust with water.
Perhaps I should switch to a language everything understands.
Shrieking through the air on a wave of Red Tide, the mechanical tentacles splinter into a thousand blades in an instant, aiming for Adelyde.
Her machine gun overheated during the fight with Rusalka, and her cannon cannot activate in time. Adelyde has no choice but to hurl herself away from the barrage.
The cable chains move almost simultaneously with the blades, but they are targeting you instead.
Taking the Sefirah from her is the same as taking you. She'll trade it for you without a second thought.
You've already caused me enough trouble as it is.
Your imagination leaves much to be desired.
Despite the looming danger, both you and Adelyde are unexpectedly calm, because you already prepared for this back when you were waiting for Ananke's Link to be re-established.
A fully-formed plan is transmitted from the other end of the M.I.N.D. connection.
(From what you've shared, every attack from you and Gray Raven was ineffective on Arius back in Port Podesta.)
(His half of the "Understanding" Sefirah lets him discern every attack's trajectory and countermeasure. To him, your bullets might as well be standing still.)
(And if we want to suppress "Understanding", this is the perfect site to do it.)
Her gaze sweeps across the dark mechanical dome before settling on the brilliant streams of Ananke rays within the cube.
(Because this Ananke was built specifically for "Understanding".)
(There's one more card we can play. The power of this other half of the Sefirah might just be enough to match his.)
(We'll have double insurance. You draw him toward the convergence point of the Ananke rays, and I'll hold the Sefirah. We'll get a shot whichever one of us he targets.)
Something molten stirs behind her eyes.
(I know the risks of touching the Sefirah. I won't use it unless there's absolutely no other choice.)
(The moment you see any sign of me losing control, point Ananke at me. Don't hesitate.)
(I don't point weapons at my allies.)
(I'll do my best to avoid that.)
(I have no proof of this, but... I don't think Ananke will hurt me.)
(It's not a weapon. Its power comes from the connection of people's beliefs. As long as we resonate with that belief, it will protect us.)
You lunge backward and step into a stream of brilliant gold light.
The chains flying at your face jolt to a sudden stop at the edge of the light. They hover there, acting like a snake recoiling from flame.
Quite nimble, aren't you? What is this, hide and seek?
Go ahead and hide in there forever. I have all the time in the world.
With a wave of his hand, he tears the spike panels from the chamber that houses the Sefirah Engine, bending the metal like fabric and flinging them toward you.
Adelyde's covering fire from afar gives you just enough window to weave between the light streams and slip past Arius' strike by a hair.
You are getting worn down, and yet Arius has not moved near the Ananke rays at all.
(We can't keep this up and win.)
Like Arius said, this has always been about the "Understanding" Sefirah.
Then, the only thing that can force his hand is the Sefirah.
There's no textbook answer in a real firefight. Intel gets you as far as the deployment phase. After that, you trust your gut.
You've got the instinct. Trust it.
Adelyde, throw the Sefirah back into Ananke!
Right before the Sefirah leaves Adelyde's hand, the world splits into endless shards, like a mirror shattering into pieces when struck at a single point.
The Ascendant surfaces from every shard of the broken mirror, impossible to pinpoint, and impossible to avoid.
His glacial power bears down from above, pinning your body and soul in place like a specimen under glass.
I don't play by the rules. I make the rules. What makes you think you could ever threaten me?
A crimson longsword materializes in his hand. Just one step, and he immediately crosses a thousand broken shards, appearing before you.
The blade flashes, and calamity strikes.
The sound of shattered armor is dry and sharp. The red-and-black Construct shudders as the blade goes through her.
Adelyde stands between you and the agent. The longsword runs clean through her side, and her vital fluid trickles down, indistinguishable from the crimson of her coating.
The cannon stands beside her, completely unscathed.
Neither the people I protect, nor the weapons I protect them with... can afford to be damaged.
Barely, but... you kept up with me for a moment.
He turns toward the opened Sefirah container on the ground with murder in his eyes.
So you stole power from the Sefirah after all.
The Sefirah belongs to all of humanity. The thief here... is you!

Adelyde grips the crimson blade that is running through her frame, and luminous blue branches of the Phylotree erupt from her hand. Wild and relentless, they coil tight around the hooded figure across from her.
She raises her half-destroyed right hand, drawing the container toward her and stuffing her half of "Understanding" inside before hurling it to you.
The Sefirah's pure glass-blue is stained with a jarring smear of dark red.
The power of the "Understanding" Sefirah she forced herself to wield is now tearing into her M.I.N.D.
Yet she has pushed your Mind Beacon away, hiding it as far from the Sefirah's power as possible.
Arius' command of "Understanding" isn't complete either. The power I've drawn should buy us a little time.
Your squad will be here soon. They can pick me up.
<color=#ffffffff><size=50>There's no room for hesitation on the battlefield.</size></color>
<color=#ffffffff><size=40>and the right move is to trust your partner's judgment</size></color>
There's no room for hesitation on the battlefield. Her plan is sound, and the right move is to trust your partner's judgment and get moving. The sooner reinforcements arrive, the better. But...
I won't leave you to take on the Consciousness Tide alone. I'm staying.
I know Ananke. I should be with you.
You think I'm out of options just because I can't move?
The mask covers so much of his face that you cannot be sure if there are eyes behind it. And yet, at this very moment, a silver-white gaze shoots through the mask toward you.
What story do you carry, I wonder... and how much use will you be to me?
The pale, sun-lit figure cuts into the night sky.
Arius has nothing but contempt for the silence around him, for a blinding radiance is about to rise from his hands and carry everyone toward the same perfect future.
He tilts his head back, raises his hand, and then—
A pair of crystal-red eyes, their irises etched with the pattern of crosshairs, stare down at him from the darkness, cold and unblinking, roiling with blood and tears.
The man freezes, as more eyes appear in the night sky around that crimson gaze.
Two are gold and red, fiery and passionate, radiant as dawn.
Two are rose hued, delicate and clear, still as a mirror.
Two are pale blue, flame-tinged, causality beheld.
Each pair of them belongs to someone who has walked through fire with you.
Every pair of them bears the mark of a forged bond and shared convictions.
They stand guard over the borders of your mind, holding this night sky fast and making it impenetrable.
They declare their judgment to the intruder with their gaze:
The world spins, and you find yourself on one knee, holding your head in your hands. Having your mind forcibly invaded never feels good.
Adelyde braces herself beside you. The sword that was lodged in her side is gone, but a small dark-red pool has gathered at her leg.
Her head is held high, her gaze fixed forward, but her expression is hollow.
She is still there. Her M.I.N.D. trembles within the Consciousness Tide's all-consuming blue light, yet her grip on your Mind Beacon holds. She has not yielded.
Arius stands in silence, holding both halves of the "Understanding" Sefirah in his hands. Their faint light mirrors each other, and they breathe with the same rhythm.
I once poured every last drop of my human intelligence into it, and still "Understanding" eluded me.
But after I've offered my life and explored <phonetic=Punishing Virus>answers beyond humanity</phonetic>, it has finally embraced me back.
His voice breaks on the last word, sounding almost reverent.
My truth... be whole through me.
He brings his palms together, combining the two halves of the helix.
The two cleanly-fractured faces draw closer... an inch... half an inch... contact—
There is no surge of light, no resonance, and no miracle.
The two halves of Sefirah rest quietly against each other, like two ordinary crystals that happen to glow.
He draws on the power and access remaining in his chest, pulling on the Red Tide and channelling everything into his hands.
The power slides past the edges of the Sefirah, not even leaving a mark.
Arius looks down. His long hair drops.
I have conquered life and death, time and space, the purest and the most corrupt of powers...
What gives you the right to stop me—
Arius, once the iron fist of the Transatlantic Economic Community, twice the bringer of global catastrophes...
He lets every last hint of composure fall away, and screams at his dead friend with a twisted expression of anguish.
But there is no one left here to listen.
In the echo of his scream, a thunderous roar rises, like a great beast stirring back to life.
Supporting herself with the weapon that has been with her since childhood, Adelyde clenches her jaw and forces herself up despite her trembling knees.
Commandant, aim Ananke at both Arius and me at the same time.
The web of strings named Eternity resonates with your call, and every soul woven into it sings as one.
Ananke's Link blazes with light, and countless rays burst forth at once in the next instant, piercing through both Arius and Adelyde's bodies.
Within the golden web and the surging Consciousness Tide, the memories Adelyde holds most dear are being torn apart shard by shard.
(Pull back Ananke's web with all you have to anchor Adelyde's M.I.N.D.)
(Not a single shard can slip away!)
Keep your right foot back and your knees bent. Engage your core.
You need to know what you're fighting for.
Adelyde finds her footing, takes a step forward, and her entire body erupts in a shower of sparks.
What if it's something beyond your power to change?
Many great feats began simply because someone wanted it very badly.
She hauls her cross cannon off the ground and holds it in her arms.
The moments she fought side by side with her younger self.
The moments she triumphed with her friends beneath a sky full of confetti.
The moments when comets and fireworks lit the path ahead.
Filled with tears and laughter, the memories explode with the energy of a dying star, and light floods back into Adelyde's hollow eyes in that moment.
Two trails of blood-red tears streak down her face, burning like fire.
My vision's going, Gray Raven. Help me aim.
Don't worry. I've anchored your mind and all your memories.
The cannon burns with a terrifying crimson light, trained on the Ascendant caught in the web.
Arcs of electricity dance across the weapon as the force from the charging weapon sends Adelyde's hair billowing.
Arius, Dominik was never the only one standing in your way.
You scorn humanity's will, mock their connections, disregard their lives...
You are the person furthest from "Understanding".
And that is why you are not worthy!
A brilliant blaze erupts from the cannon straight toward Arius, carrying with it her unwavering resolve.
The beam of light coils like a dragon, devouring the silver Ascendant whole.
Arius curls his fingers from within the beam, his face contorted. But before the Punishing Virus creations he so despised could even respond, half his body begins to melt away.
I only came to check on your progress, so imagine my surprise when I find our hero of the hour looking a little worse for wear.
Spider silk drops from the Red Tide residue clinging to the ceiling, plucking what remains of Arius free from the beam with uncanny lightness and speed.
Tightly and densely, the silk begins to spin a black hole.
A hand, pale as icy jade, reaches out from the black hole and gives the spider silk a flick, and the silk begins to drag the Ascendant in.
Besides, I'm rather fond of this body. I'm not quite ready to give it up just yet.
"Understanding" may not be usable just yet, but at least it's all accounted for. Consider the mission of restoring it your reward, Arius.
Shall I find a way to lift your spirits?
The voice murmurs on, unhurried and distant, as Arius fades into the black hole.
A chilling pair of golden eyes you have seen before glisten in the dark.
With a snap of her fingers, the spider silk, the black hole, and the agent vanish without a trace, as if a layer of image has been removed.
A commotion grows louder as the door bursts open.
You turn away from your squad immediately, just in time to see Adelyde's eyes close as she crumples to the ground.
